text:
mia: Quick heads-up — A/B run for v2.1-int4 (10% traffic) finished. Long-doc MRR down 3.2% vs v2.0 fp16, but p50 latency down 28% :chart_with_downwards_trend: :rocket:
raj: Oof. Did you slice by seqlen and cohort? where's the drop concentrated?
mia: Yes — it's almost entirely on seqlen >2000 and "legal-longform" slice. Short answers and summaries look fine.
sloane: What's our current automatic-fallback rule? Is 2% MRR drop still the threshold?
kevin: Current rule: fallback if delta.MRR > 2% on any watchlist slice for 5 continuous mins OR if overall p<0.95. But we also consider latency gains + cost savings in a composite signal.
mia: Thinking proposal: don't auto-fallback if latency gain >20% and cost/unit drops >15% unless slice MRR_drop > 3% sustained 10m. Also add kv-warmup mismatch check.
raj: Can we express that in the gate config? Something like:
```
gate:
  trigger:
    - slice_mrr_drop: {percent: 3, window_min: 10}
    - overall_confidence: {p: 0.95}
  exemptions:
    - latency_gain_pct > 20 and cost_delta_pct < -15
  actions:
    - notify: # deploy-alerts
    - autofallback: true
```
kevin: looks reasonable, but we need to quantify "cost_delta_pct" from real token-unit economics (inc KV recall lower token count...).
deploy-bot: Canary started: v2.1-int4 @ 10% (4990001200). Metrics stream: https://internal.redwood/streams/4990001200 :link:
sloane: :eyes: we should also run a shadow of v2.0 with kv-warmup on the same traffic to see if warmup reduces the long-doc regression.
mia: Agreed. Action items: 1) pause promotion; 2) reduce live canary to 5% and run 2x shadow with kv-warmup + longer burn (30m) on the legal-longform slice; 3) compute composite econ metric and decide threshold. I'll open a follow-up thread with sample slices and eval config.
raj: SGTM. If we still see >3% on that slice after warmup, auto-fallback on and roll back.
kevin: I'll add cost/econ calc to the gate and push config PR.
mia: Thanks. tagging @sloane for eval pairing. :thumbsup:
